The Future with Will, Going to, The Present Continuous and The Simple Present
Remember there are four different tenses you can use to talk about the future.
When you talk about things that are not decided or when you make a decision at the moment of speaking for the future, you use the modal <span class="italic">will.
When you ask about intentions, you use <span class="italic">be going to.
When you talk about things that are arranged, on the agenda or booked for the future, you use the <span class="strong">Present Continuous tense.
When you talk about schedules, you use the <span class="strong">Simple Present.

Remember a gerund is a noun made from a verb by adding "-ing". It is an action verb that is acting as a noun. The noun refers to an activity instead of a person or thing. Gerunds are written in their -ing form. You can use a gerund as the subject or the object of your sentence. They can also come after certain prepositions in a sentence.

From: k.lenard@mail.com
To: danielle_wilkinson@WXBJ.com
Subject: Thank You

Dear Ms Wilkinson,

Thank you very much for taking time out of your busy schedule to meet with me Tuesday and discussing how to be successful in the working world.
I appreciated your insight regarding the ways I can apply some of my coursework and skills to contribute to my future endeavors. Additionally, your advice and information makes me feel like I am on the right track and will help me further my job search.

I am grateful for the contacts you suggested to me. As you recommended, I connected with Don Urbanite, the editor of the publication you mentioned, and we have an appointment in two weeks. I sincerely appreciate you giving me his contact information. I will let you know how the meeting goes and will keep you up-to-date on my job search efforts. I especially found it helpful learning about the various job responsibilities you have had and appreciated you sharing your background experiences from starting out with the station to your current position as programming coordinator. Taking your advice, I'm going to set goals for myself. I would not have thought of developing and strengthening my skills even further in a particular area, but after our discussion, I'm committed to working on this in the future and finding my niche. Thank you again for your time and valuable assistance.

I'm looking forward to talking with you again in the future.

Regards,
Kristi Lenard
